newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria says foreign reserves rise.
newsitem.headline: Algeria says foreign reserves rise.

text.p: Algeria's Central Bank governor Abdelwahab Keramane said on Sunday that foreign currency reserves were at more than $3.5 billion this year, the highest since 1981.
"The reserves exceeded...$3.5 billion," said Keramane, quoted by the official Algerian news agency APS.

Keramane, who was addressing the government-appointed Transitional National Council -- which acts like a parliament -- said that in 1981 the reserves were high because crude oil prices surged in the fighting then between Iraq and Iran.
The reserves amounted to $2.5 billion at the end of March compared with $2.11 billion at the end of December 1995.

The government had said in the summer that Algerian oil prices had risen to an average of $20.20 per barrel in the first five months of the year against $17.90 per barrel in the same period last year.
